summary: Split a permutation of 0..n-1 into the maximum number of chunks that, sorted individually and concatenated, give the sorted array.
mainInsight: In a permutation of 0..n-1, a chunk can end at index i exactly when the maximum value seen so far equals i: then the prefix contains precisely the values 0..i.

approaches.name: Prefix max == index (greedy)
approaches.summary: Track the running max; count a chunk whenever max == i.
approaches.interviewRelevance: Your approach; the expected answer for this version.

approaches.name: Monotonic stack of chunk maxima
approaches.summary: Merge chunks while the new element is smaller than a previous chunk's max.

personalSolution.notes: Optimal for the permutation version; the stack approach handles the general version II.

cards.explanation: A prefix of a permutation holds exactly 0..i only if its largest value is i, so each such index closes a chunk.

promptVariants: Why does max == i imply the prefix is exactly {0..i}?
cards.answer: The prefix has i + 1 distinct values from 0..n-1 whose maximum is i; there are only i + 1 values in 0..i, so the prefix must contain all of them. Sorting it yields 0..i in place, so a chunk boundary is valid after i.
cards.explanation: Every valid boundary is found by a single pass.

Why does counting every index with best == i give the maximum number of chunks?
What happens for an already sorted array?
cards.answer: Every index where the prefix is exactly {0..i} is a valid cut, and using all valid cuts maximises the number of chunks (cuts are independent). For a sorted array best == i everywhere, so the answer is n.

cards.explanation: Cuts after index 0, 2 and 4 give the chunks [0], [2,1] and [4,3]; a cut after index 1 or 3 would leave an unsorted prefix.

incorrectOptionExplanations.5: Five chunks would need every element to be in its sorted position, but 2 and 1 are swapped.
incorrectOptionExplanations.2: Three independent chunks exist, so two is too few.
incorrectOptionExplanations.1: One chunk is always possible, but more cuts are valid here.
